name: cobble
summary: Setts: rounded stones bedded in mortar, laid by hand and never flat.
why: Depth 0.45, the deepest anything in this project declares, above bark's 0.35. It is
earned rather than chosen: the joints between setts are real gaps a centimetre or two
deep, the art draws them as near-black lines, and the whole reason a cobbled street
reads as cobbles rather than as a photograph of cobbles is that the light falls into
them. This is the best case the read-relief-from-luminance approach has anywhere.
Roughness 0.80. Stone worn by feet, not polished by them - a sett is walked on at one
point and rained on everywhere else.
Range 0.12, high: the crowns of the stones are burnished and the joints hold grit.
Cast, because a laid street has no direction the light cares about.
